question: Can a perception lead and an equally informed conventional analyst complete and challenge this review workflow, and what effort, disagreements and decision-relevant errors does it expose?
purpose: Development workflow rehearsal; neither efficacy benchmark nor prospective study
population: The entire exact previously exposed development package selected by the binding request; retain every window and unavailable occurrence
prior_exposure_basis: Coordinator-established premise, not verified by preparation; the actual development run must bind its retained exposure history
selection: No new cohort, seed, held-out claim or case substitution
observational_unit: One completed staged workflow on this fixed package; windows, captures and objects are not independent replicates
participants: Two independent unassisted discovery reviewers, Engine analyst, competent conventional analyst, independent adjudicator; not yet assigned
staging: Lock participant competence, exposure histories, roles, review tools, effort definitions and common release procedure before review
Deliver identical neutral observations separately; complete and lock both discovery records before either sees assisted evidence or the other's record
Check custody and externally verify actual independence and exposure order; a tool pass is not release permission

Prepare and bind one common later packet of full annotations and anonymized predictions; keep configuration mapping private, retain identical deliveries, and do not substitute the operator binding report for this packet
Give both analysts identical staged evidence and assumptions, including all original discoveries, assisted proposals and joint reference alternatives when those exist
Lock each analyst's conclusion and source identities before cross-method comparison
Independently adjudicate disagreements, preserve initial outputs and corrections, and account for all effort

conventional_comparator.tools: Analyst-selected competent conventional calculations, scripts, matching or optimization libraries; record exact versions
conventional_comparator.allowed_mathematics: Same matching, paired-loss identity, partial-identification bounds and joint alternatives as the Engine
conventional_comparator.information: Identical evidence bytes at identical logical stages; equal access to permitted expert clarification
conventional_comparator.restriction: No other method's conclusion before own conclusion is locked
conventional_comparator.selection: Do not replace a comparator because it matches or outperforms the Engine

outcomes: Reported completion or exact blocker for each role and stage
Supported decision and interval, assumptions, unresolved observations and proposed next observation
Initial disagreements and independently adjudicated consequential errors, separated from preference differences
Person time by role and preparation, review, integration, calculation, adjudication and repair category
Compute elapsed time and memory, separate from person time, with missing measurements explicit
consequential_error_definition: An independently supported correction changes a declared decision, invalidates a reported enclosure or reveals an omitted decision-relevant assumption, observation, alternative or population member
negative_results_to_retain: A competent reviewer cannot use the package or cannot support the requested physical interpretation
The enclosure remains unresolved after usable review
Both methods reach equally supported conclusions with comparable or lower conventional effort
The Engine adds repair or integration burden without a demonstrated decision benefit
analysis: Descriptive side-by-side account on the fixed rehearsal; no significance test, effect estimate, speedup claim or generalization from one workflow
unknowns: No absence from empty proposals, no zero from missing effort, no independence from distinct handles, no physical truth from a valid certificate
relationship_to_study: Does not modify or freeze the proposed 60-scene study; any revised prospective procedure needs its own versioned contract before selection
